title: Bidirectional A*: Find the fastest streets in Edinburgh
description: Watch Bidirectional A* race from both start and goal across Edinburgh’s street graph, dramatically shrinking the search space. The visualization shows how consistent heuristics guide two fronts until they meet on a shortest path.
ig_caption:
🗺️✨ **Bidirectional A*** in **Edinburgh (New Town)** — two search waves, one optimal route. 

In graph terms, the street map becomes a weighted graph (intersections = nodes, roads = edges). **Bidirectional A*** runs A* forward from the start and simultaneously backward from the goal, using heuristics to estimate remaining distance; the key win is meeting in the middle instead of exploring outward from only one side. 📉💡

Algorithmically, each frontier prioritizes nodes by **f(n)=g(n)+h(n)**, but now both directions share the work—when the forward and backward explorations intersect (or the best combined cost is proven), we reconstruct the shortest path. This typically reduces expansions and improves responsiveness on large real-world road networks. 🧠⚡

👉 Want me to test it with different heuristics (Manhattan vs. geodesic) or compare against Dijkstra/standard A*? Drop a comment and **follow** for more real-map algorithm visualizations!

By meeting in the middle, it reduces unnecessary expansions while still using the A* scoring rule (cost so far + heuristic estimate) to reach an optimal path. 📍
